You may have heard that Republicans have quietly started to count North Carolina out. You may be wondering how we're responding, and what we're doing in the final eight days to finish this race strong. So I want to give you an honest update on where this race stands, and explain why we can't get comfortable just yet. And why you shouldn't either. I know how easy it is to get swept up in the polls and take a lead for granted. I'm not asking you to ignore the numbers or the trends. But they only tell part of the story, and a few key facts need to be understood alongside them. | | ---|---|--- Just this month, President Obama's top strategist, David Plouffe, weighed in on what's at stake in this race. His message was simple: "We have to win the ones we have to win." North Carolina is one of those races. Campaign veterans and journalists alike have long seen this race as our best chance to flip a Senate seat this year, and the first step in taking back the Senate majority. It's also a hard state to win. North Carolina hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate in 2008, Obama carried it that year but lost it in 2012, and races here historically come down to the margin of error, no matter what the polls say. Roy himself had polls showing him up by double digits in 2016 and only won by 10,000 votes. So if our best chance at flipping a U.S. Senate seat is within our reach, in a state that is historically difficult for Democrats to win, why would we take our foot off the gas now? I want us to wake up on November 4th knowing we did everything in our control to flip this seat. We will win this race on the margins, and we'll lose it with complacency. That's why we're using every one of these last eight days to keep talking to voters, keep organizing in communities big and small, and keep fighting for the future of North Carolina. Polls don't mean anything without an organizing effort that gets people to the ballot box. And that takes resources. name: Sen. Jeff Bridges
subject: "Every Democrat I can find!"
body:
I met Cliff at the Delta Farmers Market, about an hour south of Grand Junction.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/9620e9969aa6/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10379755?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/o7QKfMcRuPg?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
I met Cliff at the Delta Farmers Market, about an hour south of Grand Junction. Cliff made beautiful little wooden boxes, and I picked one up for Kit. After introducing myself as a candidate for State Treasurer, Cliff leaned back and with narrowed eyes asked, “Democrat or Republican?”
In one of the most Republican parts of the state I answered, “Democrat.”
He looked at me for a bit and replied, “I’ve voted Republican my whole life. This year, I’m voting for every Democrat I can find!”
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/RF0Q8btVHFL?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | Cliff’s story repeated itself over and over on our Democratic bus tour. We traveled 1,876 miles—same as the year Colorado entered the Union! Different towns, different people, but one concern met us at every stop: **our cost of living crisis is crushing Colorado families.**
Housing. Utility bills. The struggle to earn a good life. As State Treasurer, I can’t solve that on my own, but I can put Colorado’s money to work at home by investing in:
* Housing working people can actually afford
* Renewable energy that lowers utility bills
* Infrastructure that brings good-paying jobs to Colorado

Two weeks to go. Plenty left to do. And many more miles still ahead. If you can, I’d appreciate your help as we finish strong.
---
| [Donate](https://us.list-manage.com/dFLU0ib5Z6v?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
---
| | And make sure to get your ballot in early!
Talk soon,
PS Joe Neguse might be the wittiest member of Congress, with no shortage of unclaimed property jokes on the bus. 😂
---

Welcome back! -- it has been nearly a hundred years since a party named Conservative governed British Columbia. The government that won on October 24 did not run on hospices. But one campaign promise carries more moral weight than the rest of the ballot combined: no government will force MAiD into a sanctuary hospice. The change it unlocks starts in one building.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4987f4c4-9fc3-4ab7-a676-aa97f1997292?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In Ladner, British Columbia, there is a ten-bed building where the dying were safe from the question. For a decade the Delta Hospice Society ran the Irene Thomas Hospice under a covenant old-fashioned enough to read as radical: we will manage your pain, and we will not manage your exit. The society built that hospice with roughly nine million dollars of donated money -- not one cent of public money -- and staffed it with people who saw a difference between caring for a patient and killing one. In late 2019 its board resolved that medical assistance in dying, MAiD, would not be performed on the premises. That resolution was treated as the crime.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2f914620-e31e-446e-8d12-545348dc596a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The sentence came in installments. Fraser Health delivered ultimatums, then the government's own news release announced the end of the service agreement; on February 25, 2021, about $1.5 million a year in funding stopped. On April 15, 2021, the Irene Thomas Hospice reopened under the direct control of Fraser Health -- name unchanged, MAiD now carried out inside. The society's two buildings, the hospice and the Harold and Veronica Savage Centre for Supportive Care, were expropriated. Valued at $8.5 million. Compensation paid: zero. The courts blessed every step. Blandness is how confiscation dresses: a government seized a charity's donor-built property because the charity declined to perform lethal injections in it.
Consider what that sequence implies about priorities. A province that could not guarantee access to palliative care -- the Canadian Hospice Palliative Care Association has spent years documenting that most Canadians who want it cannot get it -- found the lawyers, the lease clauses and the resolve to clear out the one hospice that refused euthanasia, as neatly as if it were a grow-op. And when the society's members answered with democracy -- 76 percent voting to write the euthanasia-free covenant permanently into their constitution -- the state's response was to keep what it had taken. Civil society made its argument. The government confiscated the premises.
Delta is a window, not an anomaly. Canada legalized assisted death in 2016 with promises of narrowness. By 2023, 15,343 people were dying by MAiD each year -- 4.7 percent of all deaths in the country, among the highest rates in the world. Parliament removed the "reasonably foreseeable death" guardrail in 2021, and has twice postponed eligibility for the mentally ill -- now set for 2027 -- while palliative care remains a patchwork in every review. Ottawa calls all this choice. In Delta, British Columbians learned what the choice was actually worth: an option for the patient, an ultimatum for the hospice.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/403187e5-f56d-4b4e-bbe3-699bfe97196a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The NDP has governed British Columbia for nine years, and the hospice threads the whole reign. John Horgan's government took it; David Eby -- who spent those years as Attorney General and then Premier -- never gave it back. Nine years is long enough to teach a province a lesson, and the lesson was received by every charity, church and care home with a conscience and a lease: your property is secure until your opinions interfere. Exiled at home, Delta Hospice did the only thing left to a dispossessed charity. It went house-hunting in Alberta -- a B.C. charity publicly shopping for a province willing to let it keep its own mission.
Then came the snap election. On September 22, Premier Eby sent British Columbians to the polls. On October 24 they gave the province to the BC Conservatives under interim leader Lorne Doerkson, the self-described guy from Williams Lake -- a majority, and the first government under a party actually named Conservative in nearly a century. In that campaign the party made a pledge with Delta written all over it, championed by Dr. Anna Kindy, a physician re-elected to the new caucus: _**no government will force MAiD into a sanctuary hospice**_. That pledge is now a mandate. And the promise the society has kept alive on its Road to Sanctuary page -- build the sanctuary hospice to honour and affirm our patients' lives, and care for them until their natural end -- has a home again. In Delta. Not Alberta.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5ce44262-1586-415c-ae03-8a43c410cbcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Here is what is being restored, because precision is the difference between an argument and a press release. Nobody is obliged to choose a sanctuary hospice. Assisted dying remains legal, and a British Columbian who wants it can still get it -- presumably under the new government too. What returns are two things the old government treated as its own property. The first is conscience: the right of a care provider to say "I will not do this," and mean it. The second is property itself: $8.5 million given in trust by donors on the strength of a covenant, taken because the covenant was inconvenient. A government that will seize a building to enforce an orthodoxy will seize anything. A donor who watches learns to give nothing. For nine years, British Columbia ran that experiment.
The verdict: the NDP's MAiD settlement was not pluralism. It was a monopoly with a ribbon on it -- the state not merely permitting a death option, but disciplining a dissenting charity, confiscating its assets and calling the seizure a service standard. That is not medicine. It is not tolerance. It _was_ power, mislabelled.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1791edc4-0f8d-4aa7-b651-7eb7f4a6097f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

clean_body: Nine years of NDP medicine in British Columbia -- and the hospice Delta is finally allowed to build. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? Nine years of NDP medicine in British Columbia -- and the hospice Delta is finally allowed to build. | | | Oct 26 | | | | | | | | | | | | Welcome back! -- it has been nearly a hundred years since a party named Conservative governed British Columbia. The government that won on October 24 did not run on hospices. But one campaign promise carries more moral weight than the rest of the ballot combined: no government will force MAiD into a sanctuary hospice. The change it unlocks starts in one building. | | ---|---|--- In Ladner, British Columbia, there is a ten-bed building where the dying were safe from the question. For a decade the Delta Hospice Society ran the Irene Thomas Hospice under a covenant old-fashioned enough to read as radical: we will manage your pain, and we will not manage your exit. The society built that hospice with roughly nine million dollars of donated money -- not one cent of public money -- and staffed it with people who saw a difference between caring for a patient and killing one. In late 2019 its board resolved that medical assistance in dying, MAiD, would not be performed on the premises. That resolution was treated as the crime. | | ---|---|--- The sentence came in installments. Fraser Health delivered ultimatums, then the government's own news release announced the end of the service agreement; on February 25, 2021, about $1.5 million a year in funding stopped. On April 15, 2021, the Irene Thomas Hospice reopened under the direct control of Fraser Health -- name unchanged, MAiD now carried out inside. The society's two buildings, the hospice and the Harold and Veronica Savage Centre for Supportive Care, were expropriated. Valued at $8.5 million. Compensation paid: zero. The courts blessed every step. Blandness is how confiscation dresses: a government seized a charity's donor-built property because the charity declined to perform lethal injections in it. Consider what that sequence implies about priorities. A province that could not guarantee access to palliative care -- the Canadian Hospice Palliative Care Association has spent years documenting that most Canadians who want it cannot get it -- found the lawyers, the lease clauses and the resolve to clear out the one hospice that refused euthanasia, as neatly as if it were a grow-op. And when the society's members answered with democracy -- 76 percent voting to write the euthanasia-free covenant permanently into their constitution -- the state's response was to keep what it had taken. Civil society made its argument. The government confiscated the premises. Delta is a window, not an anomaly. Canada legalized assisted death in 2016 with promises of narrowness. By 2023, 15,343 people were dying by MAiD each year -- 4.7 percent of all deaths in the country, among the highest rates in the world. Parliament removed the "reasonably foreseeable death" guardrail in 2021, and has twice postponed eligibility for the mentally ill -- now set for 2027 -- while palliative care remains a patchwork in every review. Ottawa calls all this choice. In Delta, British Columbians learned what the choice was actually worth: an option for the patient, an ultimatum for the hospice. | | ---|---|--- The NDP has governed British Columbia for nine years, and the hospice threads the whole reign. John Horgan's government took it; David Eby -- who spent those years as Attorney General and then Premier -- never gave it back. Nine years is long enough to teach a province a lesson, and the lesson was received by every charity, church and care home with a conscience and a lease: your property is secure until your opinions interfere. Exiled at home, Delta Hospice did the only thing left to a dispossessed charity. It went house-hunting in Alberta -- a B.C. charity publicly shopping for a province willing to let it keep its own mission. Then came the snap election. On September 22, Premier Eby sent British Columbians to the polls. On October 24 they gave the province to the BC Conservatives under interim leader Lorne Doerkson, the self-described guy from Williams Lake -- a majority, and the first government under a party actually named Conservative in nearly a century. In that campaign the party made a pledge with Delta written all over it, championed by Dr. Anna Kindy, a physician re-elected to the new caucus: no government will force MAiD into a sanctuary hospice. That pledge is now a mandate. And the promise the society has kept alive on its Road to Sanctuary page -- build the sanctuary hospice to honour and affirm our patients' lives, and care for them until their natural end -- has a home again. In Delta. Not Alberta. | | ---|---|--- Here is what is being restored, because precision is the difference between an argument and a press release. Nobody is obliged to choose a sanctuary hospice. Assisted dying remains legal, and a British Columbian who wants it can still get it -- presumably under the new government too. What returns are two things the old government treated as its own property. The first is conscience: the right of a care provider to say "I will not do this," and mean it. The second is property itself: $8.5 million given in trust by donors on the strength of a covenant, taken because the covenant was inconvenient. A government that will seize a building to enforce an orthodoxy will seize anything. A donor who watches learns to give nothing. For nine years, British Columbia ran that experiment. The verdict: the NDP's MAiD settlement was not pluralism. It was a monopoly with a ribbon on it -- the state not merely permitting a death option, but disciplining a dissenting charity, confiscating its assets and calling the seizure a service standard. That is not medicine. It is not tolerance. It was power, mislabelled. | | ---|---|--- This Substack is reader-supported. name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: The gap grew
body:
We turned a long shot into a dead heat. Now we need to finish it. | | | | I want to be straight with you, because you’ve earned that.

Back in April, I was down almost 7 points to Greg Abbott in the polling average. Political insiders wrote this race off. Then you showed up: you chipped in, spread the word, and proved that people all over the country believe Texas can be taken back. By October 7, we had cut that gap to just 1.3 points.

I know a lot of you saw that number and felt what I felt: we can actually do this.

But since then, the polls have moved in the wrong direction. Today, the average has me trailing Abbott by 2.7 points.

Here’s what I need you to hear: 2.7 points is not a lost race. This is one of the most competitive governor’s races in the country, and it will be decided by turnout, by organizing, and by what we do in these final days.

Two weeks ago, we were closer to beating Greg Abbott than anyone thought possible. If we let up now, we could lose this race by a margin we could have closed. I need you in this fight with me. [**Can you split $20 today between Equal Opportunity Now and my campaign to help us get back to where we were and finish the job?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142216932/656182722/1593610140?refcode=261026_gina_gap&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ODczYTllMy01MGQxLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LtaeYcnCRQpK2LlbrT9Rk3ecFkHC70cafR-HOwDwlWo=)

Early voting is already underway, and every dollar we raise right now goes straight into reaching the voters who will decide this thing. We can’t get comfortable. Not for a single day. **We have to make sure every voter hears the truth about Greg Abbott before they cast their ballot.**

Here’s just one example: a watchdog investigation just found that Abbott’s much-hyped “pause” on data center permits was never a pause at all.

Dozens of projects kept moving forward. That’s Greg Abbott: a press release for voters, business as usual for his corporate allies.

Your donation could be the difference between winning and losing. It could decide whether Texas gets four more years of Greg Abbott’s corruption or whether we take Texas back.

**[I’ve never needed your support more. Will you split $10 or $20 now between Equal Opportunity Now and my campaign so we can close this 2.7-point gap before Election Day?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142216933/656182723/1593610140?refcode=261026_gina_gap&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ODczYTllMy01MGQxLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LtaeYcnCRQpK2LlbrT9Rk3ecFkHC70cafR-HOwDwlWo=)**

# Palestine
* **Seven Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks on Monday:** Israeli attacks on Khan Younis in southern Gaza killed at least four Palestinians, including a seven-year-old girl, and wounded more than ten, while one Palestinian was killed and several others wounded Monday in a drone [strike](https://substack.com/redirect/2c49b265-3f5c-4d4c-b02b-88d7a065d984?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Rimal neighborhood of western Gaza City, according to WAFA. A separate Israeli drone strike in Deir el-Balah, central Gaza, killed two Palestinians and wounded two.
* Over the past 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks and 35 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Three bodies were recovered from beneath the rubble.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, is now 74,555 killed, with 175,727 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,559 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,608, while 845 bodies have been recovered.
* **800 Palestinians forced to flee from Shujaiya after Israel set fire to camp:** Over 800 Palestinians have been forced to displace yet again from Shujaiya, an eastern neighborhood in Gaza City, after Israeli forces set fire to a displacement camp, according to Al Jazeera.
* Israeli quadcopter drones set the camp ablaze at around 8 p.m. local time on Sunday destroying tents housing men, women, children, and the elderly.
* **Israeli operation in Hebron forcibly displaces over 3,100 Palestinians as attacks continue across the occupied West Bank:**
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces [continued](https://substack.com/redirect/71fdeec5-0a3a-46fa-8406-b07b5c00c9d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their military operation in Hebron for a fourth consecutive day Monday, conducting raids, demolitions, and mass displacement in the city, WAFA reported. Israeli forces have forced 3,171 Palestinians--488 families--to displace, local officials said. More than 70 Palestinians were detained and over 500 homes searched, while Israeli forces have closed 128 gates and established 120 military checkpoints across the governorate.
* In Al-Samu, settlers [beat](https://substack.com/redirect/24614631-f8cf-47cd-ade6-4cfea617e6d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a 58-year-old Palestinian woman outside her home, leaving her hospitalized with chest injuries. In Al-Dhahiriya, Israeli forces detained two brothers after settlers attacked them while they were grazing sheep.
* **Jenin:** Israeli forces began [bulldozing](https://substack.com/redirect/749aed26-c23f-491d-b591-8767e88a691e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinian land for an approximately 11.5-kilometer settlement road linking settlements near Arraba to others south of Jenin. Israeli forces also began demolishing agricultural and commercial structures near Haddad Tourist Village, including greenhouses, agricultural rooms, a car showroom, and a recreational park.
* **Palestinian "doctor of the poor," released after four months in Israeli detention: **Israeli authorities [released](https://substack.com/redirect/f5f5771d-44e2-47d1-a5de-c0cd8c4a391e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Dr. Mazen Al-Rantisi, 71, from Ganot prison after more than four months in detention, with visible signs of physical assault, according to the Palestinian Prisoner's Society. Al-Rantisi, widely known in the occupied West Bank as the "doctor of the poor," was arrested during a predawn raid on his Ramallah home on June 21, without his family being informed of the reason.
* Israeli media reports suggested his detention was linked to his role as chair of the Union of Health Work Committees, a Palestinian healthcare organization Israel designated an "unlawful association" in 2020.
* **Israel kills at least 14 Palestinians in Gaza over the weekend:** Six Palestinians, including two women and a girl, were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/48926172-62ab-4136-a60d-4f44b445eee8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Israeli forces in Gaza on Saturday, according to Shehab News, while eight Palestinians were killed on Sunday.
* Israel carried out two airstrikes on the the Islamic University in Gaza City, killing three security guards. Several students were also wounded, some seriously.
* "Today, we were studying in class, minding our business, while the professor was explaining. Suddenly, an airstrike hit directly beneath us, a massive explosion," Mohammed Qandil, an engineering student, told Drop Site's Abdel Qader Sabbah.
* "We came here to learn and get an education. We came to rebuild our country, the country they destroyed and devastated. Why are they attacking us here too?" Qandil asked.
* "It's a deceptive ceasefire. The war has not stopped. Israeli brutality has not stopped," Umm Rami Deeb said. **Watch the dispatch from Sabbah[here](https://substack.com/redirect/08b78f48-3573-469e-9c15-d0dd8e15d1a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [here](https://substack.com/redirect/639519a0-1dcb-44bf-9906-3defea5a12b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* In central Gaza, Israeli gunfire [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/f3446844-89be-462d-a4f5-aac63d6d4cc2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an eight-year-old girl, the sole survivor of her family following their killing in an Israeli strike in December 2023.

* **Netanyahu in tight race against Eisenkot in Israeli elections tomorrow:** Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, of the Likud party, faces a tight race as Israelis head to the polls on Tuesday for legislative elections. Netanyahu's chief rival in the campaign is former Israel Defense Forces Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, who heads a new party called Yashar. Eisenkot served in Netanyahu's war cabinet in the opening months of the genocide in Gaza.
* While serving as chief of the Israeli military's northern command, Eisenkot devised the so-called Dahiya doctrine, a military strategy of intentionally causing massive destruction to civilian life and infrastructure. It is named for the Dahiya neighborhood of southern Beirut, which the Israeli military routinely bombarded during its 2006 war in Lebanon. "What happened in the Dahiya quarter of Beirut in 2006 will happen in every village from which Israel is fired on," he [said](https://substack.com/redirect/385e929d-766a-463d-a07d-5b7ebaf7deb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2008. "We will apply disproportionate force on it and cause great damage and destruction there. From our standpoint, these are not civilian villages, they are military bases."
* **Israeli army chief challenges Netanyahu order over Iran confrontation:** Israel's top general [balked](https://substack.com/redirect/35537f2a-e6eb-45f9-965e-ce33cc80cee3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at an order from Prime Minister Netanyahu that he feared could set off a sudden confrontation with Iran two days before Tuesday's election, Israel's Channel 12 reported. The directive is unspecified.
* According to sources who spoke to the channel, military officials fear Netanyahu is trying to exploit the Iran issue to generate political momentum.
* Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz dismissed the report as "completely baseless."

# Iran
* **In unexpected diplomatic move, Saudi, Pakistani, and Turkish officials travel to Iran for talks:** Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey arrived in Tehran on Monday for [meetings](https://substack.com/redirect/71c0291c-fe15-4996-9e70-1f041de8b2de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei to discuss regional security, including Israeli actions in Palestine and Lebanon and the consequences of U.S. military attacks on Iran. It marks the first talks between Iran and the three countries since they signed the Mecca defense pact in August.
* Saudi diplomat Rayed Krimly [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e9c4465b-e7d5-4497-88a0-07624299d9f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the visit is in support of mediation efforts by Qatar and Pakistan and underscores the alliance's role in "reinforcing regional security and stability."
* Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said the meeting could pave the way for a regional security framework independent of outside powers, adding that "regional security can only be ensured by relying on the will and security considerations of the countries in the region themselves."
* Separately, Baghaei dismissed the significance of upcoming Israeli elections, calling them "a competition among different factions" to commit more crimes, aggression and killings. "It makes no difference to us who ultimately takes the helm of the Israeli regime," he said, adding that Israel brought "nothing to the region but violence and killings."
* **Iraq keeps borders closed to pressure Iran, orders arrest of Iraqi official opposing the closure:** An Iraqi court [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/a4f1cd6d-2ec5-4a94-ac19-6912463d64bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an arrest warrant Monday for Mustafa Al-Mohammadawi, head of the Maysan Provincial Council, over his threats to launch civil disobedience and block roads unless the government reopened the Al-Sheeb border crossing with Iran.
* Iraq indefinitely closed the Al-Sheeb crossing last Wednesday, citing security concerns and the need to install equipment to prevent smuggling. Pakistan also suspended trade through its Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan border crossings with Iran last week.
* The closures appear to signal growing U.S. pressure on Iran's overland trade routes, following Washington's naval blockade of the country, though neither government has publicly linked its decision to U.S. demands.
* **Oil spill off UAE coast widens, satellite images show:** An oil spill from a damaged tanker off the coast of the United Arab Emirates is growing, according to Reuters citing satellite imagery, with dark layers of oil spreading at sea and along the coastline of the northern Umm Al Quwain emirate.
* The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment has announced that all beaches and coastal areas around the city of Umm Al Quwain have been temporarily closed, while access to Al Hamriyah Beach in neighboring Sharjah has also been shut down as a precaution.
* Authorities have not named the tanker involved in the incident or said what caused the spill. But experts told Reuters that the spill was coming from a tanker called the Gem No.2, which was reportedly hit by an unidentified projectile last month, causing a fire that was later extinguished.

# Yemen
* **Saudi-led coalition carries out strikes in Yemen as Ansarallah claims attacks on airport, military bases, and oil infrastructure:** The Saudi-led coalition has [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/ab9ea43e-be27-4c74-8799-be132adea539?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a series of attacks targeting Ansarallah-controlled areas of Yemen, the coalition spokesperson said on Monday. The coalition claimed to have destroyed five tunnels used to store ballistic missiles, four missile launchers, and a missile storage facility. It also claimed its strikes destroyed two missile launchers in Sana'a, including one allegedly used in the attack on the Saudi capital. Sana'a-based media outlets said airstrikes hit a solar power system and a water well in the capital on Monday.
* Ansarallah targeted Riyadh's airport Monday with a ballistic missile, the group's spokesperson [said](https://substack.com/redirect/14bcf93e-4296-4078-8306-0e05229a09f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--which Saudi forces said they intercepted. Ansarallah also claimed drone attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pumping stations.
* On Sunday, Ansarallah said it [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/dad4200d-5766-4621-b9d3-a5b936f629af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) dozens of ballistic missiles in three operations on Sunday targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait, and a Saudi border guard naval base in Jizan. The group also [targeted](https://substack.com/redirect/0f34d1f2-93a5-41a5-8033-0e02a7fda1f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Saudi-backed military positions and weapons depots in Aden and Lahj in Yemen with ballistic missiles, and claimed to have shot down a Saudi Wing Loong II reconnaissance and attack drone over Taiz.
* **Egyptian parliament authorizes Sisi to send military reinforcements to Saudi Arabia if requested:** Egypt's parliament [approved](https://substack.com/redirect/fa7ce9b9-0aa1-4fa8-b346-2847d6f7f777?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a request from President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to authorize the deployment of defensive military reinforcements to Saudi Arabia if requested by the kingdom, Al Arabiya reported.
* **Over half of Taiz 's hospitals and medical centers shut down amid Ansarallah siege:** Nearly 52% of hospitals and medical centers in Yemen's Taiz have been forced out of service amid the Ansarallah siege and ongoing attacks, according to the Yemeni Women's Empowerment Foundation.
* Six kidney dialysis patients have died, while 1,280 others face treatment interruptions. Twenty maternity clinics have closed, and shortages threaten 192 intensive care patients and 154 newborns in incubators.
* More than 250 civilians have been killed or wounded in recent shelling, sniper fire, and attacks on ambulances, according to Yemen's Saudi-backed government.
* Young people in Taiz [told](https://substack.com/redirect/258e0da0-2c62-4544-9f2a-c78793a866b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Sky News they have received little military support from anti-Ansarallah factions as the group's forces besiege the city. "They tell us to come with our own Kalashnikovs and give us 20 bullets in a plastic bag. And tell us to the go the front: go, kill, go!" a young resident told the outlet.
* **Saudi-coalition strikes kill 21, wound 30 in Yemen:** Saudi airstrikes [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/fd50f015-e7a7-4b0b-8a6b-3c4e085dc4df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 21 people and wounded 30 across five Yemeni areas--Sana'a, Hamdan, Taiz, Hodeidah, and Saada--in 24 hours, according to figures from Yemen's Ansarallah-led government reported Saturday. The vast majority of the dead are women and children, with at least nine children killed and seven wounded.

# U.S. News
* **Obama, Trump attend dueling rallies in Michigan; Trump spouts Islamophobia to stir his base:** At a Port Huron rally in support of Republican Senate nominee **Mike Rogers** nine days before the midterms, President Donald Trump baselessly [called](https://substack.com/redirect/fd547bb5-b1db-49c1-b680-01d995ca9f83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Democratic Senate nominee **Abdul El-Sayed** a Muslim Brotherhood member and warned that if "Abdul and the Democrats win, they will open the floodgates and invite hordes of jihadis to our shores." He also said that anyone with El-Sayed's background "would be screened and unable to get a seat on an airplane." El-Sayed has repeatedly disavowed the Brotherhood, saying, "My name and my faith are not the reason you can't afford your gas."
* Former President **Barack Obama** [told](https://substack.com/redirect/2ed9c0e8-1f44-41a1-b64b-b2b34725edcc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a crowd in Detroit on Saturday that El-Sayed is "fighting for change, real change, change that will bring an end to this war." He added, "What is radical about that?"
* The Black vote has become a focus in the Senate campaigns: El-Sayed underperformed in Detroit, which is 75% Black, in the primary against Rep. **Haley Stevens**. A YouGov poll estimates that he will win 84% of Black voters and Mike Rogers will win 11%, while a late-September Fox News poll put Rogers's Black support at 22%.
* On NBC's Meet the Press, Rogers was confronted about his support for the Muslim Brotherhood in 2012, when he said he was open to working with its "moderate members." He declined to directly answer the question.
* **U.S. military gives SpaceX access to precise space-tracking data, raising conflict-of-interest questions** : The Space Force [signed](https://substack.com/redirect/6ac8eae1-0ca2-4c8a-88df-7da3a9453dc8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a contract granting SpaceX "enhanced" access to Space Command's High Accuracy Catalog, a first for a commercial company. The government gets access to Starlink's Stargaze sensors in return for the access. The Department of Government Efficiency, under **Elon Musk** , attempted to gut the federal government's nascent Traffic Coordination System for Space and to privatize the capacity to monitor space traffic.
* **NYC set to sign no-bid deal with Israeli tracking company:** New York City Mayor **Zohran Mamdani 's** police department is [poised](https://substack.com/redirect/1a8d0cac-f468-4e0a-b295-54fbe0659c5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to sign a three-year, $750,500, no-bid contract with Israeli surveillance firm Cognyte for FalcoNet, an AI-driven device that mimics a cell tower to track phones and can be mounted on police cars and drones or hidden in a backpack, the New York Daily News reported. Though the software would ostensibly require a warrant for cell-phone interceptions, civil liberties advocates have warned about the potential for the technology to be used against people who are not targets.

* **Trump says U.S. will "take care of Cuba"; Rubio urges Cubans to partner with CIA: **President Trump told a Florida rally on Friday that the U.S. will deal with Cuba "on our way back from Iran" and then send Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** in "to finish up the deal."
* Rubio urged those "who seek to create positive change" on the island to "seize this opportunity" through "a discrete [sic] partnership with the CIA," he [said](https://substack.com/redirect/531c9504-bc3e-4c8d-baba-ea7f5e073c16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X.
* **White House considers mass pardons for junior staff, sources say** : White House attorneys are [evaluating](https://substack.com/redirect/fa38a137-1471-4e02-b796-8d51b82b7b0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) blanket pardons for junior staffers, possibly covering all employees in areas like deportations, war, and trade, The Washington Sun reported. The Heritage Foundation and American Moment have pressed White House counsel to prepare pardons or fund expected legal fees, and conservative activist **Mike Davis** urged "very broad preemptive pardons" after Sen. **Elissa Slotkin** said congressional probes should make young Republicans think twice about joining the administration.
* **Blanche defends DOJ suit to block automatic certification of Alaska 's Senate result if Republican candidate loses:** On CNN on Sunday, Attorney General **Todd Blanche** [said](https://substack.com/redirect/19b7304a-3156-4c9e-a07b-b2b575d7280f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "we're not laying any groundwork for the president" to overturn the outcome of Alaska's Senate election. He said that the Justice Department only seeks to "certify" that the law is not violated. The suit, filed Thursday and ordered by Trump, claims that two of the names on the ballot--Sen. **Dan Sullivan** , the Republican incumbent, and retired teacher **Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.** --could confuse voters. The DOJ hasn't said how that could be determined, given the secret ballot. In August's primary, Sen. Sullivan won over 68,000 votes to the other Sullivan's 4,107.
* **SNAP enrollment has fallen 13% since the One Big Beautiful Act, straining food banks and meal programs** : Enrollment in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) [dropped](https://substack.com/redirect/a13a5e31-ea47-4606-8da2-a6d2a58bb901?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from 41.6 million in July 2025 to 36.5 million in June 2026, after the program's work requirements were expanded and its allowances for people without dependents contracted under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Arizona's enrollment is down 50%.
* Advocates note that work requirements converged with a tightening job market. The Food Bank Council of Michigan's helpline calls more than tripled, forcing a temporary suspension, and Houston's independent district lost free-meal eligibility at 26 schools because fewer students are on SNAP.
* **U.S. presses Mexico for deeper cooperation against cartels:** The U.S. recently laid out a path for U.S. security personnel to accompany Mexican forces in operations inside Mexico, the New York Times [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/8b3a5d43-bd1c-4ca1-943c-0fa8a33ab71e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The U.S. also requested closer intelligence-sharing with Mexico. Mexico has repeatedly said that joint operations and U.S. drone strikes within its borders are violations of its sovereignty, and officials said that Mexico remains "adamantly" opposed to U.S. forces operating on its soil. Mexican President **Claudia Sheinbaum** has also refused U.S. requests to arrest Mexican politicians.
* **AIPAC 's shell game: **AIPAC is funding elections to the tune of millions of dollars through shell PACs seemingly devoted to issues including women's and reproductive rights, The Lever reported in a new investigation. [Read the full article here](https://substack.com/redirect/95ef75ad-1228-41e8-8a83-70d2c9a142a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

# Other International News
* **Lula re-elected president of Brazil, defeating far-right Fl avio Bolsonaro:** President of Brazil Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva**** was [re-elected](https://substack.com/redirect/08a0b4ef-cfc6-435c-850a-3c2c0e3feae9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sunday in a tight runoff vote against Flavio Bolsonaro, a far-right challenger and the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Lula, who won by a margin of over four million votes, thanked Brazilians for their support. Bolsonaro said the election result was "inexplicable" and demanded its annulment.
* **Serbian student-led movement ousts right-wing leader Vu čić, wins big in parliament:** The right-wing Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić was defeated in a Sunday election, ending his decade in power. A student-led movement against political corruption--which Vučić has described as foreign interference--was a decisive factor in his defeat. The Student List, an electoral slate connected to the protests, is expected to win at least 135 seats in the 250-seat parliament, displacing Vučić's party as the majority.
* **The Guardian: U.S. military "weaponizing" El Niño in Somalia: **U.S. drone strikes in southern Somalia are driving civilians toward a floodplain just as a strengthening El Niño is forecast to intensify weather events this month, The Guardian [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/697b7c56-7fcd-41df-8e31-6649a3397a2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Residents described rising water levels in the River Juba, bodies in the streets, and flattened homes. A source monitoring the situation said the offensive is "exploiting El Niño as a weapon of war to push the population into flood-prone areas." The U.S. military has denied wrongdoing.
* **Remains located in Haiti during search for missing Salvadoran soldiers:** Doctors [examined](https://substack.com/redirect/77d9541a-1755-47d0-8501-baa8aa1aaa72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) human remains in Haiti to determine whether they were the bodies of the four Salvadoran soldiers who vanished after being ambushed by armed gangs last week, the New York Times reported. Three people familiar with the situation told the Times that the bodies were badly burned and not easily identifiable. El Salvador President Nayib Bukele said that the remains were not those of the missing soldiers. Last week, he sent hundreds of special forces to Haiti to find the men and threatened to "finish the gangs off" if the country's personnel were not returned alive.
* **North Korea accuses South Korea of fabricating DMZ blast, places howitzers on border:** On Monday, North Korea positioned three mobile howitzer units on the border, according to "a Reuters witness" on the scene, the newswire [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/75567c59-c95c-4711-b198-06bd19bf9635?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In a letter sent to the UN Security Council on Sunday, North Korea blamed South Korea for a September landmine explosion in the Demilitarized Zone that wounded three South Korean soldiers. South Korea, which blames the attack on North Korean mines and sent a letter of its own to the UN last week, has proposed military talks to "mutually confirm the precise location" of their shared border.
* **Jordan arrests three suspected of deadly church attack:** Jordanian security forces [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/4cc52d4c-d29b-4cb8-9c09-e2902fdb1bbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three suspects in connection with the attack on a Greek Orthodox church in western region of Karak that killed at least nine people and wounded 40 others during a funeral last week. The attack was carried out by three members of a single family that lives in the area, Maj. Gen. Obeidallah Al-Maaytah, director of the Jordanian Public Security Directorate, said Monday. The suspects were driven by "extremist ideology," he said, but he added that the suspects did not plan the attack or have ties to "outside parties."
* **Machado returns to Venezuela after more than 10 months in exile:** The Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Coria Machado returned to Venezuela after 10 months of exile, she [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/0afaa3f4-f1df-4810-a43a-65e7f3484a50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sunday. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that "U.S.-supported reconciliation talks" made her "safe return" possible. He called on all political actors to respect ongoing talks between the government and the opposition. Machado's return could destabilize the U.S.-backed political order of interim leader Delcy Rodriguez.
* **RSF attacks power stations, causes outages across southeastern Sudan:** Rapid Support Forces (RSF) strikes on power stations in four southeastern states in Sudan have caused "severe damage" to them and cut power across the region, the state electricity company [said](https://substack.com/redirect/deba9082-9cfb-4622-a375-d5aca77482ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The outages stretch across about half of the territory held by the RSF.
* **Amnesty: Gunmen kill at least 40 in Nigerian village:** Gunmen [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/12ba705e-64be-4e61-9c18-f4dc2c9f8f79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least 40 people in an attack on a village in the northeastern Nigerian state of Taraba, Amnesty International said. Armed gangs known as "bandits" have conducted numerous attacks in northern Nigeria, raiding villages, kidnapping people for ransom, and stealing livestock.
* **Algeria authorizes army deployment to Niger, first foreign troop mission since 1973** : Algerian lawmakers unanimously [approved](https://substack.com/redirect/8ea6dbae-ee5f-4225-ae21-e5dcc6f8ba7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the deployment of National Army troops to northern Niger, near the Libyan border, on Sunday. It is not clear when the deployment will begin. It will be the first Algerian troop deployment outside of its borders since 1973, when it dispatched units to support Egypt's war against Israel.

Monday, October 26, 2026 -** Palestine : Seven Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks on Monday. 800 Palestinians forced to flee from Shujaiya after Israel set fire to camp. Israeli operation in Hebron forcibly displaces over 3,100 Palestinians as attacks continue across the occupied West Bank. Israel kills at least 14 Palestinians in Gaza over the weekend. Saudi-coalition strikes kill 21, wound 30 in Yemen. U.S. : Former President Barack Obama, President Donald Trump attend dueling rallies in Michigan; Trump spouts Islamophobia to stir his base. The Guardian: U.S. military "weaponizing" El Niño in Somalia. Remains located in Haiti during search for missing Salvadoran soldiers. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Seven Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks on Monday: Israeli attacks on Khan Younis in southern Gaza killed at least four Palestinians, including a seven-year-old girl, and wounded more than ten, while one Palestinian was killed and several others wounded Monday in a drone in the Rimal neighborhood of western Gaza City, according to WAFA. A separate Israeli drone strike in Deir el-Balah, central Gaza, killed two Palestinians and wounded two. Over the past 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks and 35 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Three bodies were recovered from beneath the rubble. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, is now 74,555 killed, with 175,727 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,559 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,608, while 845 bodies have been recovered. 800 Palestinians forced to flee from Shujaiya after Israel set fire to camp: Over 800 Palestinians have been forced to displace yet again from Shujaiya, an eastern neighborhood in Gaza City, after Israeli forces set fire to a displacement camp, according to Al Jazeera. Israeli quadcopter drones set the camp ablaze at around 8 p.m. local time on Sunday destroying tents housing men, women, children, and the elderly. Israeli operation in Hebron forcibly displaces over 3,100 Palestinians as attacks continue across the occupied West Bank: Hebron: Israeli forces their military operation in Hebron for a fourth consecutive day Monday, conducting raids, demolitions, and mass displacement in the city, WAFA reported. Israeli forces have forced 3,171 Palestinians--488 families--to displace, local officials said. More than 70 Palestinians were detained and over 500 homes searched, while Israeli forces have closed 128 gates and established 120 military checkpoints across the governorate. In Al-Samu, settlers a 58-year-old Palestinian woman outside her home, leaving her hospitalized with chest injuries. In Al-Dhahiriya, Israeli forces detained two brothers after settlers attacked them while they were grazing sheep. Jenin: Israeli forces began Palestinian land for an approximately 11.5-kilometer settlement road linking settlements near Arraba to others south of Jenin. Israeli forces also began demolishing agricultural and commercial structures near Haddad Tourist Village, including greenhouses, agricultural rooms, a car showroom, and a recreational park. Palestinian "doctor of the poor," released after four months in Israeli detention: Israeli authorities Dr. Mazen Al-Rantisi, 71, from Ganot prison after more than four months in detention, with visible signs of physical assault, according to the Palestinian Prisoner's Society. Al-Rantisi, widely known in the occupied West Bank as the "doctor of the poor," was arrested during a predawn raid on his Ramallah home on June 21, without his family being informed of the reason. Israeli media reports suggested his detention was linked to his role as chair of the Union of Health Work Committees, a Palestinian healthcare organization Israel designated an "unlawful association" in 2020. Israel kills at least 14 Palestinians in Gaza over the weekend: Six Palestinians, including two women and a girl, were by Israeli forces in Gaza on Saturday, according to Shehab News, while eight Palestinians were killed on Sunday. Israel carried out two airstrikes on the the Islamic University in Gaza City, killing three security guards. Several students were also wounded, some seriously. "Today, we were studying in class, minding our business, while the professor was explaining. Suddenly, an airstrike hit directly beneath us, a massive explosion," Mohammed Qandil, an engineering student, told Drop Site's Abdel Qader Sabbah. "We came here to learn and get an education. We came to rebuild our country, the country they destroyed and devastated. Why are they attacking us here too?" Qandil asked. "It's a deceptive ceasefire. The war has not stopped. Israeli brutality has not stopped," Umm Rami Deeb said. Watch the dispatch from Sabbah and . In central Gaza, Israeli gunfire an eight-year-old girl, the sole survivor of her family following their killing in an Israeli strike in December 2023. Netanyahu in tight race against Eisenkot in Israeli elections tomorrow: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, of the Likud party, faces a tight race as Israelis head to the polls on Tuesday for legislative elections. Netanyahu's chief rival in the campaign is former Israel Defense Forces Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, who heads a new party called Yashar. Eisenkot served in Netanyahu's war cabinet in the opening months of the genocide in Gaza. While serving as chief of the Israeli military's northern command, Eisenkot devised the so-called Dahiya doctrine, a military strategy of intentionally causing massive destruction to civilian life and infrastructure. It is named for the Dahiya neighborhood of southern Beirut, which the Israeli military routinely bombarded during its 2006 war in Lebanon. "What happened in the Dahiya quarter of Beirut in 2006 will happen in every village from which Israel is fired on," he in 2008. "We will apply disproportionate force on it and cause great damage and destruction there. From our standpoint, these are not civilian villages, they are military bases." Israeli army chief challenges Netanyahu order over Iran confrontation: Israel's top general at an order from Prime Minister Netanyahu that he feared could set off a sudden confrontation with Iran two days before Tuesday's election, Israel's Channel 12 reported. The directive is unspecified. According to sources who spoke to the channel, military officials fear Netanyahu is trying to exploit the Iran issue to generate political momentum. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz dismissed the report as "completely baseless." Iran In unexpected diplomatic move, Saudi, Pakistani, and Turkish officials travel to Iran for talks: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey arrived in Tehran on Monday for with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei to discuss regional security, including Israeli actions in Palestine and Lebanon and the consequences of U.S. military attacks on Iran. It marks the first talks between Iran and the three countries since they signed the Mecca defense pact in August. Saudi diplomat Rayed Krimly the visit is in support of mediation efforts by Qatar and Pakistan and underscores the alliance's role in "reinforcing regional security and stability." Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said the meeting could pave the way for a regional security framework independent of outside powers, adding that "regional security can only be ensured by relying on the will and security considerations of the countries in the region themselves." Separately, Baghaei dismissed the significance of upcoming Israeli elections, calling them "a competition among different factions" to commit more crimes, aggression and killings. "It makes no difference to us who ultimately takes the helm of the Israeli regime," he said, adding that Israel brought "nothing to the region but violence and killings." Iraq keeps borders closed to pressure Iran, orders arrest of Iraqi official opposing the closure: An Iraqi court an arrest warrant Monday for Mustafa Al-Mohammadawi, head of the Maysan Provincial Council, over his threats to launch civil disobedience and block roads unless the government reopened the Al-Sheeb border crossing with Iran. Iraq indefinitely closed the Al-Sheeb crossing last Wednesday, citing security concerns and the need to install equipment to prevent smuggling. Pakistan also suspended trade through its Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan border crossings with Iran last week. The closures appear to signal growing U.S. pressure on Iran's overland trade routes, following Washington's naval blockade of the country, though neither government has publicly linked its decision to U.S. demands. Oil spill off UAE coast widens, satellite images show: An oil spill from a damaged tanker off the coast of the United Arab Emirates is growing, according to Reuters citing satellite imagery, with dark layers of oil spreading at sea and along the coastline of the northern Umm Al Quwain emirate. The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment has announced that all beaches and coastal areas around the city of Umm Al Quwain have been temporarily closed, while access to Al Hamriyah Beach in neighboring Sharjah has also been shut down as a precaution. Authorities have not named the tanker involved in the incident or said what caused the spill. But experts told Reuters that the spill was coming from a tanker called the Gem No.2, which was reportedly hit by an unidentified projectile last month, causing a fire that was later extinguished. Yemen Saudi-led coalition carries out strikes in Yemen as Ansarallah claims attacks on airport, military bases, and oil infrastructure: The Saudi-led coalition has a series of attacks targeting Ansarallah-controlled areas of Yemen, the coalition spokesperson said on Monday. The coalition claimed to have destroyed five tunnels used to store ballistic missiles, four missile launchers, and a missile storage facility. It also claimed its strikes destroyed two missile launchers in Sana'a, including one allegedly used in the attack on the Saudi capital. Sana'a-based media outlets said airstrikes hit a solar power system and a water well in the capital on Monday. Ansarallah targeted Riyadh's airport Monday with a ballistic missile, the group's spokesperson Saudi forces said they intercepted. Ansarallah also claimed drone attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pumping stations. On Sunday, Ansarallah said it dozens of ballistic missiles in three operations on Sunday targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait, and a Saudi border guard naval base in Jizan. The group also Saudi-backed military positions and weapons depots in Aden and Lahj in Yemen with ballistic missiles, and claimed to have shot down a Saudi Wing Loong II reconnaissance and attack drone over Taiz. Egyptian parliament authorizes Sisi to send military reinforcements to Saudi Arabia if requested: Egypt's parliament a request from President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to authorize the deployment of defensive military reinforcements to Saudi Arabia if requested by the kingdom, Al Arabiya reported. Over half of Taiz 's hospitals and medical centers shut down amid Ansarallah siege: Nearly 52% of hospitals and medical centers in Yemen's Taiz have been forced out of service amid the Ansarallah siege and ongoing attacks, according to the Yemeni Women's Empowerment Foundation. Six kidney dialysis patients have died, while 1,280 others face treatment interruptions. Twenty maternity clinics have closed, and shortages threaten 192 intensive care patients and 154 newborns in incubators. More than 250 civilians have been killed or wounded in recent shelling, sniper fire, and attacks on ambulances, according to Yemen's Saudi-backed government. Young people in Taiz Sky News they have received little military support from anti-Ansarallah factions as the group's forces besiege the city. "They tell us to come with our own Kalashnikovs and give us 20 bullets in a plastic bag. And tell us to the go the front: go, kill, go!" a young resident told the outlet. Saudi-coalition strikes kill 21, wound 30 in Yemen: Saudi airstrikes 21 people and wounded 30 across five Yemeni areas--Sana'a, Hamdan, Taiz, Hodeidah, and Saada--in 24 hours, according to figures from Yemen's Ansarallah-led government reported Saturday. The vast majority of the dead are women and children, with at least nine children killed and seven wounded. U.S. News Obama, Trump attend dueling rallies in Michigan; Trump spouts Islamophobia to stir his base: At a Port Huron rally in support of Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers nine days before the midterms, President Donald Trump baselessly the Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed a Muslim Brotherhood member and warned that if "Abdul and the Democrats win, they will open the floodgates and invite hordes of jihadis to our shores." He also said that anyone with El-Sayed's background "would be screened and unable to get a seat on an airplane." El-Sayed has repeatedly disavowed the Brotherhood, saying, "My name and my faith are not the reason you can't afford your gas." Former President Barack Obama a crowd in Detroit on Saturday that El-Sayed is "fighting for change, real change, change that will bring an end to this war." He added, "What is radical about that?" The Black vote has become a focus in the Senate campaigns: El-Sayed underperformed in Detroit, which is 75% Black, in the primary against Rep. Haley Stevens. A YouGov poll estimates that he will win 84% of Black voters and Mike Rogers will win 11%, while a late-September Fox News poll put Rogers's Black support at 22%. On NBC's Meet the Press, Rogers was confronted about his support for the Muslim Brotherhood in 2012, when he said he was open to working with its "moderate members." He declined to directly answer the question. U.S. military gives SpaceX access to precise space-tracking data, raising conflict-of-interest questions : The Space Force a contract granting SpaceX "enhanced" access to Space Command's High Accuracy Catalog, a first for a commercial company. The government gets access to Starlink's Stargaze sensors in return for the access. The Department of Government Efficiency, under Elon Musk , attempted to gut the federal government's nascent Traffic Coordination System for Space and to privatize the capacity to monitor space traffic. NYC set to sign no-bid deal with Israeli tracking company: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani 's police department is to sign a three-year, $750,500, no-bid contract with Israeli surveillance firm Cognyte for FalcoNet, an AI-driven device that mimics a cell tower to track phones and can be mounted on police cars and drones or hidden in a backpack, the New York Daily News reported. Though the software would ostensibly require a warrant for cell-phone interceptions, civil liberties advocates have warned about the potential for the technology to be used against people who are not targets. Trump says U.S. will "take care of Cuba"; Rubio urges Cubans to partner with CIA: President Trump told a Florida rally on Friday that the U.S. will deal with Cuba "on our way back from Iran" and then send Secretary of State Marco Rubio in "to finish up the deal." Rubio urged those "who seek to create positive change" on the island to "seize this opportunity" through "a discrete [sic] partnership with the CIA," he on X. White House considers mass pardons for junior staff, sources say : White House attorneys are blanket pardons for junior staffers, possibly covering all employees in areas like deportations, war, and trade, The Washington Sun reported. The Heritage Foundation and American Moment have pressed White House counsel to prepare pardons or fund expected legal fees, and conservative activist Mike Davis urged "very broad preemptive pardons" after Sen. Elissa Slotkin said congressional probes should make young Republicans think twice about joining the administration. Blanche defends DOJ suit to block automatic certification of Alaska 's Senate result if Republican candidate loses: On CNN on Sunday, Attorney General Todd Blanche "we're not laying any groundwork for the president" to overturn the outcome of Alaska's Senate election. He said that the Justice Department only seeks to "certify" that the law is not violated. The suit, filed Thursday and ordered by Trump, claims that two of the names on the ballot--Sen. Dan Sullivan , the Republican incumbent, and retired teacher Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. --could confuse voters. The DOJ hasn't said how that could be determined, given the secret ballot. In August's primary, Sen. Sullivan won over 68,000 votes to the other Sullivan's 4,107. SNAP enrollment has fallen 13% since the One Big Beautiful Act, straining food banks and meal programs : Enrollment in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) from 41.6 million in July 2025 to 36.5 million in June 2026, after the program's work requirements were expanded and its allowances for people without dependents contracted under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Arizona's enrollment is down 50%. Advocates note that work requirements converged with a tightening job market. The Food Bank Council of Michigan's helpline calls more than tripled, forcing a temporary suspension, and Houston's independent district lost free-meal eligibility at 26 schools because fewer students are on SNAP. U.S. presses Mexico for deeper cooperation against cartels: The U.S. recently laid out a path for U.S. security personnel to accompany Mexican forces in operations inside Mexico, the New York Times . The U.S. also requested closer intelligence-sharing with Mexico. Mexico has repeatedly said that joint operations and U.S. drone strikes within its borders are violations of its sovereignty, and officials said that Mexico remains "adamantly" opposed to U.S. forces operating on its soil. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has also refused U.S. requests to arrest Mexican politicians. AIPAC 's shell game: AIPAC is funding elections to the tune of millions of dollars through shell PACs seemingly devoted to issues including women's and reproductive rights, The Lever reported in a new investigation. . 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Lula re-elected president of Brazil, defeating far-right Fl avio Bolsonaro: President of Brazil Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva** was on Sunday in a tight runoff vote against Flavio Bolsonaro, a far-right challenger and the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Lula, who won by a margin of over four million votes, thanked Brazilians for their support. Bolsonaro said the election result was "inexplicable" and demanded its annulment. Serbian student-led movement ousts right-wing leader Vu čić, wins big in parliament: The right-wing Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić was defeated in a Sunday election, ending his decade in power. A student-led movement against political corruption--which Vučić has described as foreign interference--was a decisive factor in his defeat. The Student List, an electoral slate connected to the protests, is expected to win at least 135 seats in the 250-seat parliament, displacing Vučić's party as the majority. The Guardian: U.S. military "weaponizing" El Niño in Somalia: U.S. drone strikes in southern Somalia are driving civilians toward a floodplain just as a strengthening El Niño is forecast to intensify weather events this month, The Guardian . Residents described rising water levels in the River Juba, bodies in the streets, and flattened homes. A source monitoring the situation said the offensive is "exploiting El Niño as a weapon of war to push the population into flood-prone areas." The U.S. military has denied wrongdoing. Remains located in Haiti during search for missing Salvadoran soldiers: Doctors human remains in Haiti to determine whether they were the bodies of the four Salvadoran soldiers who vanished after being ambushed by armed gangs last week, the New York Times reported. Three people familiar with the situation told the Times that the bodies were badly burned and not easily identifiable. El Salvador President Nayib Bukele said that the remains were not those of the missing soldiers. Last week, he sent hundreds of special forces to Haiti to find the men and threatened to "finish the gangs off" if the country's personnel were not returned alive. North Korea accuses South Korea of fabricating DMZ blast, places howitzers on border: On Monday, North Korea positioned three mobile howitzer units on the border, according to "a Reuters witness" on the scene, the newswire . In a letter sent to the UN Security Council on Sunday, North Korea blamed South Korea for a September landmine explosion in the Demilitarized Zone that wounded three South Korean soldiers. South Korea, which blames the attack on North Korean mines and sent a letter of its own to the UN last week, has proposed military talks to "mutually confirm the precise location" of their shared border. Jordan arrests three suspected of deadly church attack: Jordanian security forces three suspects in connection with the attack on a Greek Orthodox church in western region of Karak that killed at least nine people and wounded 40 others during a funeral last week. The attack was carried out by three members of a single family that lives in the area, Maj. Gen. Obeidallah Al-Maaytah, director of the Jordanian Public Security Directorate, said Monday. The suspects were driven by "extremist ideology," he said, but he added that the suspects did not plan the attack or have ties to "outside parties." Machado returns to Venezuela after more than 10 months in exile: The Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Coria Machado returned to Venezuela after 10 months of exile, she on Sunday. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that "U.S.-supported reconciliation talks" made her "safe return" possible. He called on all political actors to respect ongoing talks between the government and the opposition. Machado's return could destabilize the U.S.-backed political order of interim leader Delcy Rodriguez. RSF attacks power stations, causes outages across southeastern Sudan: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) strikes on power stations in four southeastern states in Sudan have caused "severe damage" to them and cut power across the region, the state electricity company . The outages stretch across about half of the territory held by the RSF. Amnesty: Gunmen kill at least 40 in Nigerian village: Gunmen at least 40 people in an attack on a village in the northeastern Nigerian state of Taraba, Amnesty International said. Armed gangs known as "bandits" have conducted numerous attacks in northern Nigeria, raiding villages, kidnapping people for ransom, and stealing livestock. Algeria authorizes army deployment to Niger, first foreign troop mission since 1973 : Algerian lawmakers unanimously the deployment of National Army troops to northern Niger, near the Libyan border, on Sunday. It is not clear when the deployment will begin. It will be the first Algerian troop deployment outside of its borders since 1973, when it dispatched units to support Egypt's war against Israel. | | ---|---|--- 🎥 The War Brief | Ep. 6: Trump Threatens Global Economy, Iran Promises Broad Response, Israel Kills 29 Palestinians 📖 Sudanese Army Drone Strikes Kill Scores of Civilians in Crowded Market 🛒 for your Drop News/Not Bombs Hoodie 💬 our Whatsapp Broadcast Channel for the latest reporting, podcasts, and breaking news, delivered directly ⚠️ You can go to your to unsubscribe from the Drop Site Daily newsletter--while still getting the rest of our reporting Become a Drop Site News Paid Subscriber Drop Site News is reader-supported. body:
Our race is a toss-up, and control of the Legislature could come down to districts like ours.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/AAm7b71cMVk?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)
| | | | | | Good morning, patriot!These last 10 days have been incredibly busy as I've met with different organizations, attended events, and continued campaigning throughout Legislative District 2. If you are still holding onto an early mail-in ballot, today is the last day to mail it back, ensuring it arrives before next Tuesday’s election. If you are able to I highly recommend finding the nearest [open polling location](https://us.list-manage.com/Z4Oe3yr1JZZ?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) and walking the ballot in so you can show your ID and have it verified. An election official can verify your identity in person, allowing your ballot to bypass the signature verification process. Once they verify your ID, they will stamp your ballot envelope “ID Verified” allowing your ballot to bypass the normal signature verification process.I stopped by the Arizona Citizens Defense League's annual meeting. It's always great to be in a room with people who support our Constitution and the right to keep and bear arms. These individuals understand what is at stake for our state. Many of their members are proudly stepping up to help us maintain our legislative majority at the Capitol by encouraging others to vote in this mid-term election.I also attended the Arizona Humane Society's annual “Compassion with Fashion” annual event. As you may recall, I have successfully worked to protect animals and prevent animal cruelty alongside this passionate coalition of animal lovers. I've also championed legislation aimed at expanding opportunities for certified veterinary technicians in Arizona.As Chair of the Senate Committee on Regulatory Affairs and Government Efficiency, I welcomed the opportunity to visit a local marijuana dispensary to learn about upcoming federal rulemaking and how it may affect their current business model.I was also honored to speak with the members who make the Arizona Equal Justice Challenge possible. For the past two legislative sessions, I have helped champion legal aid funding that benefits individuals across our state.Last Thursday, I had the opportunity to tour [East Valley Institute of Technology (EVIT)](https://us.list-manage.com/Y1kuVgEJNrl?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) and see the progress they've made through legislative appropriations over the years. Demand for Career and Technical Education Districts (CTEDs) continues to grow, especially with the addition of TSMC to the Northwest Valley and the increasing need for highly skilled workers, including electricians. The last time I visited their campus was in the fall of 2023. Since then, their electrician program has grown from 40 to 400 students in a remarkably short period of time.Over the summer, I nominated our local family-owned jewelry store, [Douglas Diamonds](https://us.list-manage.com/1n_ycvb2xsn?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) as “Retailer of the Year for Legislative District 2” with the Arizona Retailers Association. I had a chance to present Ruth and Jonathan Douglas their award at the annual awards luncheon on Thursday afternoon. If you're in the Moon Valley area, I encourage you to stop by their beautiful store if you are in the market for jewelry. I missed seeing Mark Douglas at the ceremony, but he was back at the store installing new flooring and jewelry display cases. And if you're a dog lover, be sure to say hello to Copper for me while you are there!Last Thursday evening, I was invited to speak to the local Women for Gun Rights group. I hadn’t spoken to Cheryl Todd’s group since the spring of 2023 about the legislative process. I must have done an okay job because she asked me to once again explain how citizens can get involved in the legislative process and make their voices heard through the Legislature's Request to Speak (RTS) system. It's always rewarding to spend time with a group of diverse, yet like-minded individuals, especially at the end of a busy day on the campaign trail.I ended my workweek at the [Arizona Veterans Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony.](https://us.list-manage.com/G1RX4aEQ_Sl?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) It was an honor to meet and recognize some of our state's incredible veterans. Later that evening, I attended the annual gala hosted by the Goldwater Institute, where it was inspiring to be surrounded by so many liberty-loving Arizonans.After campaigning in the district, on Saturday afternoon, I attended U.S. Senator Jon Kyl's memorial service. The tributes from his son and granddaughter were deeply moving. I first met Senator Kyl while working on Capitol Hill in the 1990s. After my family moved to Arizona, he supported the launch of the Institute for Justice's Phoenix chapter by speaking at its kickoff event. At the time, I was pregnant with my son, and Senator Kyl joked that he hoped my son would share his late-April birthday. Although my son arrived in mid-April, I've never forgotten that conversation. When I decided to run for public office, Senator Kyl offered his endorsement to many of my state legislative races.Arizona has lost a true statesman, someone who understood public policy through the lens of an Arizonan and knew how to build coalitions and strategies that could successfully advance legislation._Well done, good and faithful servant._

## 🇺🇸 The Final Stretch
The next eight days will determine far more than the outcome of one legislative race.They will determine whether Arizona continues moving forward with leaders who defend constitutional freedoms, support law enforcement, promote educational opportunity, and fight for accountable government.Our opponents are spending heavily in these final days because they know control of the Legislature could come down to races like ours. As of October 22nd, out-of-state Big Labor and other left wing special interests have spent $634,715 attacking my bipartisan record and lying about my successful legislative wins.We cannot afford to let up now.We're launching our final voter-contact effort, but we need the resources to reach every persuadable voter before Election Day. Your contribution today will help fund digital advertising, voter outreach, and our get-out-the-vote operation. [Can you help us raise $14,500 by the end of today?](https://us.list-manage.com/GI1_xSTeJGI?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) Tomorrow, we will have one week until the election and will be placing our final ad buys.**If every person reading this gave just $25 today, we would have the resources needed to finish this campaign at full strength.** Please don't wait until tomorrow. These final days matter.👉 **Make your**[**contribution**](https://us.list-manage.com/178U1mfuEVr?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)**today and help us defend Legislative District 2, protect our legislative majority, and keep Arizona on the right track.****Donate Today →**[**DONATE**](https://us.list-manage.com/gQPZCyuUlEo?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)
Thank you for your support, your encouragement, and your belief in the future of Arizona. Together, we can finish strong and win on Election Day. 🇺🇸
Best,Shawnna
