Democrats have responded by launching an **"Emergency Early Vote Turnout Surge"** and are preparing to spend more than **$1 million in Maricopa County this next week alone**.They know control of the Legislature may come down to districts like ours.With approximately 65% of Arizona's voters living in Maricopa County, the final outcome of races across the state may be determined by what happens over the next few days.**Now is not the time to sit on the sidelines.**[**Please chip in whatever you can today and help us finish strong.**](https://us.list-manage.com/QKj9VlhiKjg?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) Together, we can make the difference in these final days.**Donate Today →**[**DONATE**](https://us.list-manage.com/FY0noLoGCmV?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) 🇺🇸

backing down in the fight against fascism.

color.

Rashida

A year ago, I weighed over 360 pounds.

Hey folks,
The corruption inside Trump world is starting to eat itself alive.
Trump's own Justice Department is reportedly investigating longtime ally Corey Lewandowski over whether he personally profited from his role at DHS. And Trump's response tells you everything: he keeps talking about people stealing from _him_.
* [**00:01:26**] We dig into the reported DOJ investigation of Corey Lewandowski and allegations that he personally profited while serving in a government role at DHS.
* [**00:03:44**] I explain why Trump's reaction is so revealingnand why I think loyalty, money, and the possibility of presidential pardons are central to understanding this entire ecosystem.
* [**00:06:19**] Trump reportedly starts asking questions about Lewandowski's role in a $220 million DHS advertising campaign as the fallout from Kristi Noem's tenure keeps growing.
* [**00:09:07**] We go deeper into previous reporting about Lewandowski allegedly seeking outside work while wielding enormous influence inside DHS, and the broader culture that allowed this behavior to flourish.
* [**00:11:53**] This is the part Democrats cannot forget: there's so much alleged corruption that individual scandals disappear almost immediately, and accountability has to remain a priority long after Election Day.

Corey Lewandowski is one person, but this story is about something much bigger. It's about what happens when public service becomes a vehicle for personal power and profit, and when so many scandals pile up that we stop remembering them. We cannot let that happen. **If you value independent media that keeps track, keeps digging, and keeps demanding accountability, help me keep doing this work.**

Case File No DRT-ED-UNDERGROUND · Special File · Three Miles Down
Power on America’s Biggest Grid Nearly Doubled in a Year. That Is Why Drilling Crews Are Working Three Miles Under the Utah Desert.
Wholesale electricity on the PJM grid went from $77.78 to $136.53 a megawatt-hour in twelve months. Oil is back above $100. September inflation re-accelerated to 3.7% on energy costs. The scarcest thing in the American economy is no longer a chip or a worker — it is a megawatt you can count on, and the search for it has gone underground.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
For twenty years, American electricity demand barely moved. Utilities planned around flat load, and nobody outside the industry thought about where the power came from. That era ended quietly, and the bill is now arriving in two places at once: the monthly statement on your kitchen table, and the capital budgets of every company that needs to plug something in.
The evidence board
| | What We Know
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the grid.** On May 14, 2026, Monitoring Analytics, the independent market monitor for PJM, reported wholesale power at $136.53 per megawatt-hour against $77.78 a year earlier — a 76% jump. The monitor laid the blame on data centers and on PJM’s failure to handle their surging demand. PJM had paused applications for new generation back in 2022, citing a years-long backlog.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the fuel.** Brent crude traded at $107.29 a barrel on October 13, 2026, after peaking at $118.35 on March 31 during the Strait of Hormuz crisis. September’s CPI came in at 3.7%, up from the summer, with energy the main driver; core inflation was 2.6%.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the new load.** In its Global Financial Stability Report of October 13, 2026, the IMF wrote that “free cash flows are rapidly declining as hyperscalers try to sustain large AI investment needs.” Translation: the companies building the data centers are now borrowing to pay for the power and the buildings around it.
| CHATTER
---
The counter-argument is worth stating. Deep projects are expensive, slow and failure-prone. Permits, water rights and local opposition kill more of them than geology does, and a resource that is abundant in the ground is not the same as a resource that is cheap at the meter.
| OUR THEORY
---
Scarcity has moved one link up the chain. For thirty years the bottleneck was the chip. Now it is the thing that makes the chip run — firm, round-the-clock power, sited where it is needed. Whoever can produce it closest to the load, and keep producing it at three in the morning, holds the asset everyone else has to buy.
Connected file
| | The Commodity Nobody Mines
---|---
There is a second way to look at this. Computing capacity itself is starting to behave like a raw material: priced, contracted years ahead, and fought over by buyers who cannot substitute anything else for it.
The numbers behind that buildout are getting heavy. One analysis of five hyperscalers — Oracle, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet — put more than $1.3 trillion of debt on their balance sheets, with roughly $3 trillion more allocated off them. The IMF flagged the same pattern in October, warning about “circular financing,” where one company funds another’s project in exchange for the money being spent on its own products.
Some analysts argue the companies supplying that capacity are the ones to watch, not the ones buying it.

The United States spent two decades treating electricity as a solved problem. It is now the constraint on the fastest-growing industry in the country, and the people with capital have noticed.

And if you know her really well, you know that even on her birthday, she'd rather be out knocking on doors, talking to voters, or finding some other way to keep busy. But I think she's earned a moment to reflect on what an extraordinary year it has been. | Last month, Kim won a hard-fought Democratic primary for Attorney General thanks to the incredible support of people like you. Since then, we've watched this campaign grow even stronger, with support from local and national advocacy organizations, Democratic groups, labor unions, elected leaders, and thousands of neighbors across our state who share Kim's vision for a safer and stronger Rhode Island. And through it all, Kim hasn't slowed down. She's been traveling across Rhode Island, meeting people where they are, listening to their concerns, and making the case for why we need an Attorney General who will fight for all of us. I've known Kim since we were students at Providence College. We actually played together on the national champion rugby team - Go Friars! We've built a life together and are raising three wonderful daughters in Providence, along with two new puppies! But one thing about Kim has never changed: when she believes in something, she gives it everything she's got. | I've seen that determination in our family, in her years as a prosecutor fighting for victims, and now in this campaign. And I couldn't be more proud of her. With Election Day just over a week away, I know exactly what Kim's birthday wish would be: to finish this campaign strong and earn the opportunity to serve Rhode Island as our next Attorney General. So I have a small birthday request of my own. I know how much your support means to Kim and how grateful she is to have you standing with her as we head into these final days. Thank you for believing in Kim and for being part of this journey. Sincerely, Jenna | P.S. Kim's closing ad is out today! Give it a watch ~~. | ~~ "Instagram" ~~ "Facebook" ~~ "Bluesky" "X" ~~ "YouTube" PAID FOR BY KIM AHERN FOR RHODE ISLAND ~ Want to change how you receive these emails? You can unsubscribe ~~.

name: Wes Moore
subject: Saying goodbye
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2195%2E1086043%2EQjacSE)
This is a longer email about saying goodbye, Peter, but if you don’t have time to read through, I would deeply appreciate **[a contribution to power our campaign for the final week of this election.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261026-1.lcLI8f&refcode=em-20261026-1&t=2&akid=2195%2E1086043%2EQjacSE)**
After nearly a century of operation, Valley Forge Military Academy — the place where I went to school and grew from an angry, complicated child to a confident young man — has closed.
When my mother first sent me to the Forge, she saw military school as a last resort in response to a seemingly endless chain of misbehavior, both at home and at school. At age 11, I’d already felt handcuffs on my wrists. **I was not on a path to success.**
There was no overnight miracle when I started school there, but slowly, things changed. I learned about honor, code, and service. I started to take an interest in campus life, academics, and leadership positions — and I rose up the ranks and became a first captain in command of around 800 cadets.
After graduation, I went on to study at Johns Hopkins and Oxford, deployed to Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division, ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country, and now, I serve as the 63rd governor of Maryland _and the first Black governor in the history of my state._
What saddens me most isn’t losing a place I once called home. My memories will forever live on with me.
**It saddens me that other young men like me will have one fewer avenue to challenge themselves and build their own pathway to success.**
Peter, at a time where our young men and boys are falling behind and feeling isolated, we have to offer more paths for connection and engagement.
I know Valley Forge Military Academy did that for me, and I’m determined to find ways to do that for young Marylanders today.
That includes the **Maryland Corps and Service Year Option** — the first statewide program in the country to give high school graduates a year of paid, full-time community service on the path to college or a career.
We have to help young Marylanders find the thing that guides them on a pathway to success and that inspires them to serve. **[If you support that mission, I would appreciate a donation to keep me in the fight as Maryland's governor today.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261026-1.lcLI8f&refcode=em-20261026-1&t=3&akid=2195%2E1086043%2EQjacSE)**
Elevate,
Wes
[](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261026-1.lcLI8f&refcode=em-20261026-1&t=4&akid=2195%2E1086043%2EQjacSE)
